title: Use visualizations to make a signal obvious

blocks.content: A panel runs a query, then draws the result. A chart is one way to draw it. Grafana has many more: a gauge for how close a disk is to full, a heatmap for where values cluster, a map for where in the world. The same data, drawn differently, makes a different point. When your data arrives in Grafana Cloud, you pick the picture that fits.
That's the gallery: a page of tiles, each linking to a working example of one visualization.
Next, look at three different pictures:
Find **Gauges**: how far a number is from its limit, at a glance.
blocks.tooltip: A disk filling up, a queue near overflow: this picture shows the distance to a limit in one look.

blocks.content: Find **Heatmaps**: where values cluster, over time.
blocks.tooltip: Dense spots mean many measurements landed there. Good for spotting patterns a line would hide.

blocks.content: Click **Geomap** to open working maps that plot data by location.
blocks.tooltip: Real data, real coordinates, drawn on a map.

blocks.content: When your data arrives in Grafana Cloud, you pick the picture that fits what you need to see: how close to a limit, where values cluster, or where in the world.
